key_insight: The paper proves that every choice of five positive masses yields only finitely many planar central configurations up to similarity, resolving Smale’s sixth problem for five bodies in the plane.
engineering_relevance: This gives a rigorous computational classification result for a classic nonlinear dynamical system, showing how symbolic algebra and proof assistants can certify finiteness in complex geometric models.
method: Extend the Albouy–Kaloshin strategy to analyze algebraic curves of complex solutions and their behavior at infinity.
Use valuation-balance arguments and potential-energy expansions to rule out candidate cluster diagrams for all positive masses.
Apply exact computer algebra with rational certificates, then verify remaining exceptional mass families separately, including Lean formalization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exact certificate-based exclusion of all but a few one-parameter mass families, and gives explicit counts of real configurations on two exceptional rays: 306 and 294 up to orientation-preserving similarity.
watch_item: The proof relies on delicate case analysis and exact algebraic certificates, so reproducing or extending it to larger-body systems may be computationally and formally demanding.
paper_title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies for all positive masses
